thread:
arjun: ran an nsys capture against canary runtime this evening to reproduce the p99 jitter we saw. attached a short notes blob and the raw .qdrep link from infra-bot

marta: sweet, how long was the capture and what load?

arjun: 30s captures shot across a steady 250rps sim (seq_len 512). grabbed two variants: full nsys capture + a lightweight perfetto CPU trace.

tim: curious about overhead numbers — any perf counters?

arjun: basic numbers: full nsys (all streams) added ~14% throughput degradation when running under 250rps with batching on. tail latency p99 moved +9-12ms. GPU occupancy looked lower during trace sections (scheduling stalls).

selena: 14% is hefty. did you capture kernel timeline? which kernels are hot?

arjun: yes — top kernels by GPU time: attention_kv_fwd, matmul_f16, layernorm_fwd, kv_cache_lookup. attention_kv_fwd is ~42% of captured GPU time during sample windows. there are lots of tiny kernel launches for kv_cache_lookup (hundreds per request) which balloon launch overhead in profiler windows.

marta: that aligns with batching heuristics — small requests + KV lookup storm => many tiny kernels. profiling amplifies launch latency.

selena: so question: sampling vs full trace for prod — what's our safe budget?

tim: from the runs: full trace on 1% of traffic would add ~0.14% absolute throughput cost (1% * 14% overhead) but it concentrates on the traced requests; users may see regressed tail p99 on those specific requests. so team-level SLA risk is low at 1% but on-call noise will increase.

arjun: measured sampled trace (nsys with --trace-fork, short captures triggered every 10th request with a 50ms capture window) gave ~1.8% overall throughput hit and p99 impact under +2ms. so sampling wins.

selena: practical guardrails proposal:
- default: sampled traces only (1 in N requests, configurable N per route)
- full capture: only on canaries or with oncall approval, limited to 0.1% of traffic and auto-expire
- capture duration cap: max 30s per trace, prefer 5-10s
- auto-toggle off if p99 increases >10% vs baseline during capture window

marta: additions: tag traces with model version + batch config + kv-cache state. we need to correlate small-kernel storms with KV cache misses.

arjun: implemented a lightweight wrapper that triggers nsys via subprocess for a single request and dumps minimal timeline, plus a metadata JSON. snippet:

```
nsys profile --output $OUT --force --sample=cpu --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --trace=cuda,nvtx --duration=5
```

and the request wrapper: start NVTX region around request, if sample-hit then trigger capture.

tim: also try to use nsys --sample=none with `--trace=cuda` only for GPU timeline (smaller) and combine with perfetto for CPU — that reduces overhead vs full sampling capture.

selena: how do we estimate capture storage cost? infra-bot: artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-inference-profiles/1782345678/nsys-1782345678.qdrep (2.1GB) + perfetto (120MB).

marta: 2.1GB per full trace is not acceptable at scale. need retention rules + compression + auto-parse to extract kernel timeline and discard raw.

arjun: agreed. plan:
- keep full .qdrep for 7d for oncall/debug only, then auto-delete
- parse summary into small JSON (kernel timeline aggregates) stored permanently (~<50KB)
- for production sampled traces, only store parsed summary unless flagged as incident

selena: runbook for enabling traces in prod?

arjun: proposed runbook:
1) open thread with intent + estimated budget (pct traffic)
2) run in sampled mode for 24h, collect summaries
3) if root cause unclear, escalate to canary full capture with 0.1% traffic + oncall approval
4) full captures auto-disable after 2h or if p99 > 10%

tim: add metrics to console: active_trace_fraction, trace_overhead_estimate, avg_capture_size. make them visible per-route and per-model.

marta: technical mitigation for tiny kernels: aggregate kv_cache_lookup launches into fused kernels where possible and introduce batching delay heuristics: hold requests for up to 2ms to coalesce KV lookup work. but need to measure impact on latency.

arjun: initial microbench shows coalescing 2ms reduces small-kernel count by ~60% and frees up ~18% GPU time in our sample. downside: median latency +1.3ms. tradeoff seems worth it for some low-latency-tolerant routes.

selena: ok action items:
- arjun: land sampled-trace wrapper + parsing pipeline (PR by EOD tomorrow)
- tim: add console metrics and UI flags for trace budgets
- marta: prototype KV lookup coalescing in runtime (A/B on canary)
- infra-bot: ensure artifacts upload + short retention policy (7d) for .qdrep and permanent small JSON summaries

arjun: I'll post the parsed summary JSON to the incident dashboard and link back here. thanks all :thumbsup:

infra-bot: artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-inference-profiles/1782345678/summary.json (4.6KB)
